title: The white bull instructed in a secret — born a bull, became a man, built the vessel
summary_md: Out of the white line that runs from Adam a deliverer is raised, and he is not left to work it out for himself. One of the four is sent to him: *And one of those four went to that white bull and instructed him in a secret, without his being terrified: he was born a bull and became a man, and built for himself a great vessel and dwelt thereon; and three bulls dwelt with him in that vessel and they were covered in.* (1 Enoch 89:1). The white bull is Noah, and the three bulls with him are Shem, Ham, and Japheth. The secret he is taught is the one Genesis spells out in plain words: *Make thee an ark of gopher wood; rooms shalt thou make in the ark, and shalt pitch it within and without with pitch.* (Genesis 6:14), and then the reason for it, *And, behold, I, even I, do bring a flood of waters upon the earth, to destroy all flesh, wherein is the breath of life, from under heaven; and every thing that is in the earth shall die.* (Genesis 6:17). Peter counts the same household that Enoch saw covered in: *Which sometime were disobedient, when once the longsuffering of Elohim (God) waited in the days of Noah, while the ark was a preparing, wherein few, that is, eight souls were saved by water.* (1 Peter 3:20). And Jasher remembers who closed the door: *And Noah and his household, and all the living creatures that were with him, came into the ark on account of the waters of the flood, and Yahuah (the Lord) shut him in.* (Jasher 6:15). Notice the order of it. The bull is chosen out of the herd and told the secret before a drop of water falls. He did not save himself by his own wit; he was instructed, he obeyed, and he was shut in and kept.
note: 88:4 words live at 89:1 (live 88 has only three verses); re-cited, prose reworked, canon witnesses kept.

title: The torrents and fountains — the cattle perish, the vessel floats, the earth dries
summary_md: The Flood comes from above and from below at the same time. Enoch sees the roof of heaven first: *And again I raised mine eyes towards heaven and saw a lofty roof, with seven water torrents thereon, and those torrents flowed with much water into an enclosure.* (1 Enoch 89:2), and then the ground itself: *And I saw again, and behold fountains were opened on the surface of that great enclosure, and that water began to swell and rise upon the surface, and I saw that enclosure till all its surface was covered with water.* (1 Enoch 89:3). Genesis says it the same way, windows above and fountains beneath: *In the six hundredth year of Noah's life, in the second month, the seventeenth day of the month, the same day were all the fountains of the great deep broken up, and the windows of heaven were opened.* (Genesis 7:11). The whole herd of that corrupted earth goes under: *And all the cattle of that enclosure were gathered together until I saw how they sank and were swallowed up and perished in that water.* (1 Enoch 89:5). Only the vessel rides it out: *But that vessel floated on the water, while all the oxen and elephants and camels and asses sank to the bottom with all the animals, so that I could no longer see them, and they were not able to escape, (but) perished and sank into the depths.* (1 Enoch 89:6). Then the torrents are shut off and the earth comes back into view: *And again I saw in the vision till those water torrents were removed from that high roof, and the chasms of the earth were levelled up and other abysses were opened.* (1 Enoch 89:7), *Then the water began to run down into these, till the earth became visible; but that vessel settled on the earth, and the darkness retired and light appeared.* (1 Enoch 89:8). Genesis has Noah lifting the cover and seeing the same thing: *the waters were dried up from off the earth: and Noah removed the covering of the ark, and looked, and, behold, the face of the ground was dry.* (Genesis 8:13). Yahusha (Jesus) took this very scene as the picture of his own coming: *And knew not until the flood came, and took them all away; so shall also the coming of the Son of Adam be.* (Matthew 24:39). The herd swallowed, the elect kept in the vessel, the darkness retiring and the light appearing. It ain't new.
note: All five quotes moved to 89:2-8 (live 88 is three verses); the invented 88:12 'covered with verdure' replaced by the live 89:7-8; Jubilees 5:31 dropped (not in the live pool); Genesis 8:13 kept from the old text.

title: The sheep saved from the wolves, the Lord who comes down, and the sea
summary_md: The deliverer is one of the oppressed flock, saved out of the wolves' hands before he is ever sent back to them: *And a sheep which had been saved from the wolves fled and escaped to the wild asses; and I saw the sheep how they lamented and cried, and besought their Lord with all their might, till that Yahuah (Lord) of the sheep descended at the voice of the sheep from a lofty abode, and came to them and pastured them.* (1 Enoch 89:16). That is Moses, carried off to Midian, and it is the Lord of the sheep himself who comes down at the cry of the flock. Then the sheep is called and sent: *And He called that sheep which had escaped the wolves, and spake with it concerning the wolves that it should admonish them not to touch the sheep.* (1 Enoch 89:17), and a second sheep goes with him into the wolves' assembly, which is Aaron at Pharaoh's court. The wolves do not let go, and so the Lord of the sheep leads the flock out himself: *And Yahuah (Lord) of the sheep went with them, as their leader, and all His sheep followed Him: and His face was dazzling and glorious and terrible to behold.* (1 Enoch 89:22). At the water the picture is Exodus to the letter: *And that sea was divided, and the water stood on this side and on that before their face, and their Lord led them and placed Himself between them and the wolves.* (1 Enoch 89:24), and *And I saw till all the wolves who pursued those sheep perished and were drowned.* (1 Enoch 89:27). Moses wrote it this way: *And Moses stretched out his hand over the sea; and Yahuah (LORD) caused the sea to go back by a strong east wind all that night, and made the sea dry land, and the waters were divided.* (Exodus 14:21), and *the children of Yashar'el (Israel) went into the midst of the sea upon the dry ground* (Exodus 14:22). Read the two side by side and the thing Enoch wants you to see is plain: Moses is a sheep, and a saved one, but the one who stands between the flock and the wolves at the sea is the Lord of the sheep in person.
note: Invented 89:16/89:18 replaced by the live 89:16, 89:17, 89:22, 89:24, 89:27; Exodus 14 witnesses kept.

title: Sinai, the covenant, and the house built for the Lord of the sheep
summary_md: The sheep that led the flock out becomes a man and builds a house: *And I saw in this vision till that sheep became a man and built a house for Yahuah (Lord) of the sheep, and placed all the sheep in that house.* (1 Enoch 89:36). That is the tabernacle, the dwelling where the flock is gathered under its Shepherd, and it comes after the mountain. Enoch sets the Lord of the sheep before them on the rock first: *And after that I saw Yahuah (Lord) of the sheep who stood before them, and His appearance was great and terrible and majestic, and all those sheep saw Him and were afraid before His face.* (1 Enoch 89:30). That is Sinai as Moses recorded it: *And mount Sinai was altogether on a smoke, because Yahuah (LORD) descended upon it in fire... and the whole mount quaked greatly.* (Exodus 19:18). There the flock is made a people set apart: *if ye will obey my voice indeed, and keep my covenant, then ye shall be a peculiar treasure unto me above all people... ye shall be unto me a kingdom of priests, and an holy nation* (Exodus 19:5-6). The covenant is the very ground of their being a flock at all, and the blood seals it: *And Moses took the blood, and sprinkled it on the people, and said, Behold the blood of the covenant, which Yahuah (LORD) hath made with you concerning all these words.* (Exodus 24:8). The house that Enoch sees raised in the wilderness later stands in stone: *it came to pass in the four hundred and eightieth year after the children of Yashar'el (Israel) were come out of the land of Egypt... that he began to build the house of Yahuah (LORD).* (1 Kings 6:1). First the Lord on the mountain, then the covenant, then the house to hold the sheep. The order never changes.
note: CHECK: the mechanical draft re-cited the house verse to 89:36; prose that leaned on the old 'saved sheep' and the old 89:23 'eyes opened' line mended; 89:30 added for the mountain scene.

title: The sheep go astray, are forsaken, and given to the wild beasts
summary_md: After the house and the tower, the flock turns away, and Enoch is shown what that costs: *And after that I saw that when they forsook the house of Yahuah (Lord) and His tower they fell away entirely, and their eyes were blinded; and I saw Yahuah (Lord) of the sheep how He wrought much slaughter amongst them in their herds until those sheep invited that slaughter and betrayed His place.* (1 Enoch 89:54). The beasts are the nations, and the flock is handed to them: *And He gave them over into the hands of the lions and tigers, and wolves and hyenas, and into the hand of the foxes, and to all the wild beasts, and those wild beasts began to tear in pieces those sheep.* (1 Enoch 89:55). This is the scattering of the houses, and the canon names the first of them by king and by city: *In the ninth year of Hoshea the king of Assyria took Samaria, and carried Yashar'el (Israel) away into Assyria, and placed them in Halah and in Habor by the river of Gozan, and in the cities of the Medes.* (2 Kings 17:6). The cause was covenant-breaking, never the covenant itself: *the children of Yashar'el (Israel) had sinned against Yahuah (LORD) their Elohim (God)... and had feared other gods* (2 Kings 17:7), until *Yahuah (LORD) removed Yashar'el (Israel) out of his sight, as he had said by all his servants the prophets* (2 Kings 17:23). Ezekiel sees the same flock in the same teeth: *And they were scattered, because there is no shepherd: and they became meat to all the beasts of the field, when they were scattered.* (Ezekiel 34:5), *My sheep wandered through all the mountains... yea, my flock was scattered upon all the face of the earth, and none did search or seek after them* (Ezekiel 34:6). And the cry that goes up is the one Asaph taught the flock to pray: *Give ear, O Shepherd of Yashar'el (Israel), you that leadest Joseph like a flock; you that dwell between the cherubims, shine forth.* (Psalm 80:1). The sheep given to the beasts are not thrown away. They are scattered, and a scattered flock is one that is still counted and still waited for.
note: Invented 89:34-35 replaced by the live 89:54-55; 2 Kings, Ezekiel 34, Psalm 80 kept (Psalm 80:1 re-quoted in full from the live text).

title: The seventy shepherds who destroy more than they were commanded
summary_md: When the Lord of the sheep gives the flock over, he does not leave them unwatched. He hands them to overseers with a count: *And He called seventy shepherds, and cast those sheep to them that they might pasture them, and He spake to the shepherds and their companions: 'Let each individual of you pasture the sheep henceforward, and everything that I shall command you that do ye.* (1 Enoch 89:59), and he sets a recorder over the overseers: *And He called another and spake unto him: 'Observe and mark everything that the shepherds will do to those sheep; for they will destroy more of them than I have commanded them.* (1 Enoch 89:61). Then exactly that happens: *And I saw till those shepherds pastured in their season, and they began to slay and to destroy more than they were bidden, and they delivered those sheep into the hand of the lions.* (1 Enoch 89:65). The prophets know these shepherds by name and by habit. They feed themselves: *Son of Adam, prophesy against the shepherds of Yashar'el (Israel)... Woe be to the shepherds of Yashar'el (Israel) that do feed themselves! should not the shepherds feed the flocks?* (Ezekiel 34:2), and *the diseased have ye not strengthened, neither have ye healed that which was sick... neither have ye sought that which was lost; but with force and with cruelty have ye ruled them* (Ezekiel 34:4). Yahuah (God) answers them as Enoch's book answers them, with a reckoning: *Behold, I am against the shepherds; and I will require my flock at their hand* (Ezekiel 34:10). Jeremiah pronounces the woe, *Woe be unto the pastors that destroy and scatter the sheep of my pasture! saith Yahuah (LORD).* (Jeremiah 23:1), and Zechariah sees the worthless one judged in his own body: *Woe to the idol shepherd that leaveth the flock! the sword shall be upon his arm, and upon his right eye* (Zechariah 11:17). Every excess is written in a book before it is ever answered. The shepherds are the ones on trial here, not the sheep they were given.
note: Invented 89:45 replaced by the live 89:59, 89:61, 89:65 (the commissioning, the recorder, the excess); the judgment itself belongs to the 90:25 thread; canon witnesses kept.

title: The ram raised from the flock, and the house with the lofty tower
summary_md: Between the scattering and the exile the vision shows the kingdom. The flock is being eaten by dogs and foxes and boars until a leader is raised from among the sheep themselves: *And the dogs and the foxes and the wild boars began to devour those sheep till Yahuah (Lord) of the sheep raised up [another sheep] a ram from their midst, which led them.* (1 Enoch 89:42). That first ram forsakes its glory, and a second is anointed in its place: *And Yahuah (Lord) of the sheep sent the lamb to another lamb and raised it to being a ram and leader of the sheep instead of that ram which had forsaken its glory.* (1 Enoch 89:45). Saul, then David, in colours. The second ram drives the beasts off, and under his son the house is built: *And that house became great and broad, and it was built for those sheep: and a tower lofty and great was built on the house for Yahuah (Lord) of the sheep, and that house was low, but the tower was elevated and lofty, and Yahuah (Lord) of the sheep stood on that tower and they offered a full table before Him.* (1 Enoch 89:50). The canon dates that tower: *And it came to pass in the four hundred and eightieth year after the children of Yashar'el (Israel) were come out of the land of Egypt, in the fourth year of Solomon’s reign over Yashar'el (Israel), in the month Zif, which is the second month, that he began to build the house of Yahuah (LORD).* (1 Kings 6:1). And the ram raised out of the flock is the pattern of the one Shepherd the prophets were promised: *And I will set up one shepherd over them, and he shall feed them, even my servant David; he shall feed them, and he shall be their shepherd.* (Ezekiel 34:23), the Shepherd who says of himself, *I am the good shepherd: the good shepherd gives his life for the sheep.* (John 10:11), and who names the scattered part of the same flock, *And other sheep I have, which are not of this fold: them also I must bring, and they shall hear my voice; and there shall be one fold, and one shepherd.* (John 10:16). The leader is taken from the midst of the sheep, and the house is built for the sheep. Enoch never shows a different flock moving in.
note: The old summary's books, new house, and white bull were all invented at 89:41-50; the live 89:41-50 is Saul, David, Solomon and the temple, so the thread is re-formed on that and retitled. The books/new house/white bull are carried by the 90:20, 90:29, and 90:37 threads.

title: The great horn raised — the eyes opened and the rams run to it
summary_md: The sheep have been picked to the bone by the eagles and kites, and the few that are left are deaf and blind, until something new is born among them: *But behold lambs were borne by those white sheep, and they began to open their eyes and to see, and to cry to the sheep.* (1 Enoch 90:6). The flock will not hear them, and the ravens tear at the lambs, and then the horn comes: *And I saw till horns grew upon those lambs, and the ravens cast down their horns; and I saw till there sprouted a great horn of one of those sheep, and their eyes were opened.* (1 Enoch 90:9), *And it looked at them [and their eyes opened], and it cried to the sheep, and the rams saw it and all ran to it.* (1 Enoch 90:10). The book of the Maccabees remembers the family this sprouted from, *In those days arose Mattathias the son of John, the son of Simeon, a priest of the sons of Joarib, from Jerusalem, and dwelt in Modin.* (1 Maccabees 2:1), and the son they set at the front, *As for Judas Maccabeus, he has been mighty and strong, even from his youth up: let him be your captain, and fight the battle of the people.* (1 Maccabees 2:66). But a horn that opens the eyes of the flock and gathers the rams to itself reaches past Modin to the promise Jeremiah carried: *Behold, the days come, saith Yahuah (LORD), that I will raise unto David a righteous Branch, and a King shall reign and prosper, and shall execute judgment and justice in the earth.* (Jeremiah 23:5). The horn does not replace the sheep. It grows on one of them, cries to the rest, and they run to it because their eyes were opened to see.
note: Invented 90:1 and 90:3 replaced by the live 90:6, 90:9, 90:10 (the lambs, the horn, the rams running); Maccabees and Jeremiah kept.

title: The horn they could not break — the Lord of the sheep comes to its help
summary_md: Every bird of prey comes against the horn at once: *And those ravens fought and battled with it and sought to lay low its horn, but they had no power over it.* (1 Enoch 90:12), *And I saw till the shepherds and eagles and those vultures and kites came, and they cried to the ravens that they should break the horn of that ram, and they battled and fought with it, and it battled with them and cried that its help might come.* (1 Enoch 90:13). The help is not its own. Heaven answers the cry: *And I saw till that man, who wrote down the names of the shepherds [and] carried up into the presence of Yahuah (Lord) of the sheep [came and helped it and showed it everything: he had come down for the help of that ram].* (1 Enoch 90:14), and then the Lord of the sheep comes himself: *And I saw till Yahuah (Lord) of the sheep came unto them in wrath, and all who saw Him fled, and they all fell into His shadow from before His face.* (1 Enoch 90:15). This is the way the prophets always said the flock would be shepherded, by one the Lord sets up and stands behind: *And I will set up one shepherd over them, and he shall feed them, even my servant David; he shall feed them, and he shall be their shepherd.* (Ezekiel 34:23). The one shepherd gathers the fold that is not yet in the pen, *And other sheep I have, which are not of this fold: them also I must bring, and they shall hear my voice; and there shall be one fold, and one shepherd.* (John 10:16), and he is the one who said *I am the good shepherd: the good shepherd gives his life for the sheep.* (John 10:11). The ram's horn holds because the power behind it is not the ram's. The Lord of the sheep came down for its help, and the sheep it cried for are his.
note: Invented 90:7 and 90:10 replaced by the live 90:12-15; Ezekiel 34:23 and John 10 kept.

title: The throne in the pleasant land and the sealed books opened
summary_md: The staff falls first: *And I saw till Yahuah (Lord) of the sheep came unto them and took in His hand the staff of His wrath, and smote the earth, and the earth clave asunder, and all the beasts and all the birds of the heaven fell from among those sheep, and were swallowed up in the earth and it covered them.* (1 Enoch 90:18). Then the seat of judgment is set in the land itself, and the record that has been kept all along is opened: *And I saw till a throne was erected in the pleasant land, and Yahuah (Lord) of the sheep sat Himself thereon, and the other took the sealed books and opened those books before Yahuah (Lord) of the sheep.* (1 Enoch 90:20). Daniel was shown the same throne and the same books: *I beheld till the thrones were cast down, and the Ancient of days did sit, whose garment was white as snow, and the hair of his head like the pure wool: his throne was like the fiery flame, and his wheels as burning fire.* (Daniel 7:9), *A fiery stream issued and came forth from before him: thousand thousands ministered unto him, and ten thousand times ten thousand stood before him: the judgment was set, and the books were opened.* (Daniel 7:10). John sees the books opened at the last reckoning of the dead: *And I saw the dead, small and great, stand before Elohim (God); and the books were opened: and another book was opened, which is the book of life: and the dead were judged out of those things which were written in the books, according to their works.* (Revelation 20:12). The books in Enoch were written day by day as the shepherds destroyed, and sealed, and laid beside him. Nothing done to the flock was lost. The judgment reads back what was recorded.
note: Invented 90:12 replaced by the live 90:18 and 90:20 (staff, throne, sealed books); Daniel 7 and Revelation 20 kept.

title: The fallen stars and the seventy shepherds judged — the false shepherds reckoned
summary_md: The reckoning goes in order. The first star and all that followed it are brought up first: *And Yahuah (Lord) called those men the seven first white ones, and commanded that they should bring before Him, beginning with the first star which led the way, all the stars whose privy members were like those of horses, and they brought them all before Him.* (1 Enoch 90:21), then the overseers of the flock: *And He said to that man who wrote before Him, being one of those seven white ones, and said unto him: ‘Take those seventy shepherds to whom I delivered the sheep, and who taking them on their own authority slew more than I commanded them.’* (1 Enoch 90:22). The sentence is given in the same order: *And the judgement was held first over the stars, and they were judged and found guilty, and went to the place of condemnation, and they were cast into an abyss, full of fire and flaming, and full of pillars of fire.* (1 Enoch 90:24), *And those seventy shepherds were judged and found guilty, and they were cast into that fiery abyss.* (1 Enoch 90:25). The stars are the Watchers who left their place. The shepherds are the appointed rulers of the exile who went past their charge, and the prophets had already put the charge against them in writing: *Woe be unto the pastors that destroy and scatter the sheep of my pasture! saith Yahuah (LORD).* (Jeremiah 23:1), *Therefore thus saith Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel) against the pastors that feed my people; Ye have scattered my flock, and driven them away, and have not visited them: behold, I will visit upon you the evil of your doings, saith Yahuah (LORD).* (Jeremiah 23:2), and Zechariah's worthless shepherd gets the same sword: *Woe to the idol shepherd that leaveth the flock! the sword shall be upon his arm, and upon his right eye: his arm shall be clean dried up, and his right eye shall be utterly darkened.* (Zechariah 11:17). What goes into the fire is the misrule, the ones who took the sheep on their own authority. The sheep themselves are being gathered.
note: Invented 90:15-16 replaced by the live 90:21-22 and 90:24-25; Jeremiah 23 and Zechariah 11 kept.

title: The new house, greater and loftier — the New Jerusalem, the mountain of the house
summary_md: The old house is not repaired. It is folded up and carried away, and a greater one is set in its place: *And I saw till Yahuah (Lord) of the sheep brought a new house greater and loftier than that first, and set it up in the place of the first which had been folded up: all its pillars were new, and its ornaments were new and larger than those of the first, the old one which He had taken away, and all the sheep were within it.* (1 Enoch 90:29). And the whole flock comes home to it: *And all that had been destroyed and dispersed, and all the beasts of the field, and all the birds of the heaven, assembled in that house, and Yahuah (Lord) of the sheep rejoiced with great joy because they were all good and had returned to His house.* (1 Enoch 90:33). John saw the same house come down: *And I John saw the holy city, new Jerusalem, coming down from Elohim (God) out of heaven, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband.* (Revelation 21:2), *And I heard a great voice out of heaven saying, Behold, the tabernacle of Elohim (God) is with men, and he will dwell with them, and they shall be his people, and Elohim (God) himself shall be with them, and be their Elohim (God).* (Revelation 21:3). Micah saw it raised above every hill: *But in the last days it shall come to pass, that the mountain of the house of Yahuah (LORD) shall be established in the top of the mountains, and it shall be exalted above the hills; and people shall flow unto it.* (Micah 4:1). And Ezekiel names who the house is for, the two houses made one with the sanctuary set among them: *Moreover I will make a covenant of peace with them; it shall be an everlasting covenant with them: and I will place them, and multiply them, and will set my sanctuary in the midst of them for evermore.* (Ezekiel 37:26). Read the words Enoch chose: the ones who were destroyed and dispersed are the ones who return. The new house is bigger because the whole scattered flock is coming back into it, not because a different people moved in.
note: Invented 90:17 and reworded 90:19 replaced by the live 90:29 and 90:33; Revelation 21, Micah 4, Ezekiel 37 kept.

title: The eyes opened, the sheep gathered — the awakening of the scattered houses
summary_md: Through the whole long vision the sheep have been blind, and the last thing Enoch sees done to them is their sight given back: *And the eyes of them all were opened, and they saw the good, and there was not one among them that did not see.* (1 Enoch 90:35). It begins before the judgment, when the horn sprouts and cries: *And it looked at them [and their eyes opened], and it cried to the sheep, and the rams saw it and all ran to it.* (1 Enoch 90:10). And it ends with the whole flock inside, every one that had been lost: *And all that had been destroyed and dispersed, and all the beasts of the field, and all the birds of the heaven, assembled in that house, and Yahuah (Lord) of the sheep rejoiced with great joy because they were all good and had returned to His house.* (1 Enoch 90:33). The opened eyes are what the prophets promised for the day of the return: *Then the eyes of the blind shall be opened, and the ears of the deaf shall be unstopped.* (Isaiah 35:5), *And in that day shall the deaf hear the words of the book, and the eyes of the blind shall see out of obscurity, and out of darkness.* (Isaiah 29:18). And the gathering is the two-house gathering Ezekiel was told to speak: *And say unto them, Thus saith Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD); Behold, I will take the children of Yashar'el (Israel) from among the heathen, whither they be gone, and will gather them on every side, and bring them into their own land:* (Ezekiel 37:21), the divided houses coming up under one head: *Then shall the children of Yahudah (Judah) and the children of Yashar'el (Israel) be gathered together, and appoint themselves one head, and they shall come up out of the land: for great shall be the day of Jezreel.* (Hosea 1:11). The eyes open first, then the sheep run to the one who cried to them, then they are brought home. That is the order Enoch saw, and it is the order the awakening is walking in now.
note: Invented 90:10 and 90:18 replaced by the live 90:35, 90:10, 90:33; Isaiah, Ezekiel, Hosea kept.

title: The book written for the generations — preserve it, hand it on, add nothing
summary_md: The Epistle opens by naming what it is and who it is for: *The book written by Enoch—[Enoch indeed wrote this complete doctrine of wisdom, (which is) praised of all men and a judge of all the earth] for all my children who shall dwell on the earth. And for the future generations who shall observe uprightness and peace.* (1 Enoch 92:1). The charge behind that opening was given to Methuselah earlier in the book: *And now, my son Methuselah, all these things I am recounting to thee and writing down for thee, and I have revealed to thee everything, and given thee books concerning all these: so preserve, my son Methuselah, the books from thy father's hand, and (see) that thou deliver them to the generations of the world.* (1 Enoch 82:1), *I have given wisdom to thee and to thy children, [And thy children that shall be to thee], That they may give it to their children for generations, This wisdom (namely) that passeth their thought.* (1 Enoch 82:2). This is the Torah's own pattern for handing down the word, father to son to son's son: *And these words, which I command thee this day, shall be in thine heart:* (Deuteronomy 6:6), *And thou shalt teach them diligently unto thy children, and shalt talk of them when thou sittest in thine house, and when thou walkest by the way, and when thou liest down, and when thou risest up.* (Deuteronomy 6:7). And what is handed down is handed down whole: *Ye shall not add unto the word which I command you, neither shall ye diminish ought from it, that ye may keep the commandments of Yahuah Elohaychem (the LORD your God) which I command you.* (Deuteronomy 4:2), a fence John sets around the last book of all: *For I testify unto every man that heareth the words of the prophecy of this book, If any man shall add unto these things, Elohim (God) shall add unto him the plagues that are written in this book:* (Revelation 22:18). A book written for the generations is only any use to them if it reaches them as it was written. That is why it was given to a son with the word preserve.
note: Invented 92:1-2 and 92:14 replaced by the live 92:1 (the anchor) with the Methuselah charge quoted from 82:1-2 where it actually lives; Deuteronomy and Revelation kept.

title: Days appointed for all things — and the sinners who alter the order
summary_md: Enoch tells his children not to be shaken by the times, because the times are not in the sinners' hands: *Let not your spirit be troubled on account of the times; For the Holy and Great One has appointed days for all things.* (1 Enoch 92:2). He had already shown them what the sinners would do to the appointed order: *And in the days of the sinners the years shall be shortened, And their seed shall be tardy on their lands and fields, And all things on the earth shall alter, And shall not appear in their time: And the rain shall be kept back And the heaven shall withhold (it).* (1 Enoch 80:2), *And the moon shall alter her order, And not appear at her time.* (1 Enoch 80:4), *And the whole order of the stars shall be concealed from the sinners, And the thoughts of those on the earth shall err concerning them, [And they shall be altered from all their ways], Yea, they shall err and take them to be gods.* (1 Enoch 80:7). Daniel names the horn that sets its hand to the same thing: *And he shall speak great words against the El Elyon (most High), and shall wear out the saints of the El Elyon (most High), and think to change times and laws: and they shall be given into his hand until a time and times and the dividing of time.* (Daniel 7:25). To change the times is to lay hands on the appointed feasts, and Jubilees, given on the same mountain as the Torah, says so almost word for word: *For there will be those who will assuredly make observations of the moon–now (it) disturbs the seasons and comes in from year to year ten days too soon.* (Jubilees 6:36), and *they will go wrong as to the new moons and seasons and sabbaths and festivals, and they will eat all kinds of blood with all kinds of flesh.* (Jubilees 6:37). The blood is the oldest line of all, from the days of Noah: *But flesh with the life thereof, which is the blood thereof, shall ye not eat.* (Genesis 9:4). The sinners can confuse the calendar and hide the order from themselves. They cannot move the days the Holy and Great One appointed, and that is why Enoch says do not be troubled.
note: Invented 92:3 replaced by the live 92:2 (anchor) and the altered-order verses of 80:2, 80:4, 80:7 where the thought lives; Daniel 7:25, Jubilees 6, Genesis 9, Leviticus 17 kept.

title: The righteous one arises and walks in the paths of righteousness — eternal light, and sin seen no more
summary_md: Against the corruption of the order Enoch sets the one who rises from sleep and walks: *And the righteous one shall arise from sleep, [Shall arise] and walk in the paths of righteousness, And all his path and conversation shall be in eternal goodness and grace.* (1 Enoch 92:3). What he is given is not a lighter way but power to walk the right one: *He will be gracious to the righteous and give him eternal uprightness, And He will give him power so that he shall be (endowed) with goodness and righteousness, And he shall walk in eternal light.* (1 Enoch 92:4), *And sin shall perish in darkness for ever, And shall no more be seen from that day for evermore.* (1 Enoch 92:5). The Epistle says the same blessing plainly a little further on: *But in those days blessed are all they who accept the words of wisdom, and understand them, And observe the paths of the El Elyon (Most High), and walk in the path of His righteousness, And become not godless with the godless; For they shall be saved.* (1 Enoch 99:10). These are the two ways Moses set before the people at the Jordan: *See, I have set before thee this day life and good, and death and evil;* (Deuteronomy 30:15), *In that I command thee this day to love Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God), to walk in his ways, and to keep his commandments...* (Deuteronomy 30:16), *I call heaven and earth to record this day against you, that I have set before you life and death, blessing and cursing: therefore choose life, that both thou and thy seed may live:* (Deuteronomy 30:19). The Psalter knows the same fork in the road: *For Yahuah (LORD) knoweth the way of the righteous: but the way of the ungodly shall perish.* (Psalm 1:6). And the eternal light Enoch promises is the life Yahusha (Jesus) defined in his own prayer: *And this is life eternal, that they might know thee the only true Elohim (God), and Yahusha HaMashiach (Jesus Christ), whom thou hast sent.* (John 17:3). The paths of righteousness are the way of life, and grace is what gives a man the power to walk them.
note: Invented 92:5 and 92:12 replaced by the live 92:3-5 (the anchor) and 99:10; Deuteronomy 30, Psalm 1, John 17 kept.

title: A complete doctrine of wisdom — the law of the luminaries, exact and recorded
summary_md: The Epistle names itself at the door: *The book written by Enoch—[Enoch indeed wrote this complete doctrine of wisdom, (which is) praised of all men and a judge of all the earth] for all my children who shall dwell on the earth. And for the future generations who shall observe uprightness and peace.* (1 Enoch 92:1). A great part of that wisdom is the law of the lights, which Enoch had closed out for his son a few chapters earlier: *And now, my son, I have shown thee everything, and the law of all the stars of the heaven is completed.* (1 Enoch 79:1). It was not his own reckoning. *And the account thereof is accurate and the recorded reckoning thereof exact; for the luminaries, and months and festivals, and years and days, has Uriel shown and revealed to me, to whom Yahuah (Lord) of the whole creation of the world hath subjected the host of heaven.* (1 Enoch 82:7), *And these are the orders of the stars, which set in their places, and in their seasons and festivals and months.* (1 Enoch 82:9). This is the fourth day of creation spelled out: *And Elohim (God) said, Let there be lights in the firmament of the heaven to divide the day from the night; and let them be for signs, and for seasons, and for days, and years:* (Genesis 1:14). The seasons the lights are set for are the appointed ones, the feasts: *These are the feasts of Yahuah (LORD), even holy convocations, which ye shall proclaim in their seasons.* (Leviticus 23:4), and the Psalter keeps the same fixed order, *He appointed the moon for seasons: the sun knoweth his going down.* (Psalm 104:19). The lights that keep their stations preach without a word: *The heavens declare the glory of Elohim (God); and the firmament sheweth his handywork.* (Psalm 19:1). The calendar is not an opinion a man holds. It is a law written in the sky, shown to Enoch by the angel set over it, and recorded exactly so the feasts would fall where their Maker set them.
note: Invented 92:6-7 replaced by the live 92:1 (anchor) and the luminary law at 79:1, 82:7, 82:9; Genesis 1, Leviticus 23, Psalms kept.

title: The leaders of the stars keep their stations — and men who err by them take them for gods
summary_md: Sin has an end in this book: *And sin shall perish in darkness for ever, And shall no more be seen from that day for evermore.* (1 Enoch 92:5). Set beside that the ones who never sinned at all, the chiefs of the lights: *And the leaders of the heads of the thousands, who are placed over the whole creation and over all the stars, have also to do with the four intercalary days, being inseparable from their office, according to the reckoning of the year, and these render service on the four days which are not reckoned in the reckoning of the year.* (1 Enoch 75:1). The stars keep their course; it is men who go wrong by them: *Owing to them men shall be at fault and not reckon them in the whole reckoning of the year: yea, men shall be at fault, and not recognize them accurately.* (1 Enoch 82:5), and the error ends in idolatry: *And the whole order of the stars shall be concealed from the sinners, And the thoughts of those on the earth shall err concerning them, [And they shall be altered from all their ways], Yea, they shall err and take them to be gods.* (1 Enoch 80:7). Daniel shows the other end of the same sky, where the ones who keep and teach the order are made to shine like the lights they kept: *And many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt.* (Daniel 12:2), *And they that be wise shall shine as the brightness of the firmament; and they that turn many to righteousness as the stars for ever and ever.* (Daniel 12:3). Over those who fear the Name the true light rises: *But unto you that fear my name shall the Sun of righteousness arise with healing in his wings; and ye shall go forth, and grow up as calves of the stall.* (Malachi 4:2). The heavens keep telling it: *Day unto day uttereth speech, and night unto night sheweth knowledge.* (Psalm 19:2). The lights never led anyone astray. The ones who hide the order and teach men to worship the lights are the ones whose sin perishes in the dark.
note: Invented 92:11 and 92:13 replaced by the live 92:5 (anchor), 75:1, 82:5, 80:7; Daniel 12, Malachi 4, Psalm 19 kept.

title: The plant of uprightness and the elect of the world — what Enoch learned from the tablets
summary_md: Enoch opens the recounting with the ones it is about: *And Enoch said: 'Concerning the children of righteousness and concerning the elect of the world, And concerning the plant of uprightness, I will speak these things, Yea, I Enoch will declare (them) unto you, my sons: According to that which appeared to me in the heavenly vision, And which I have known through the word of the holy angels, And have learnt from the heavenly tablets.'* (1 Enoch 93:2). What follows is the planting itself: *And after that in the third week at its close A man shall be elected as the plant of righteous judgement, And his posterity shall become the plant of righteousness for evermore.* (1 Enoch 93:5), and the enclosure built around it: *And after that in the fourth week, at its close, Visions of the holy and righteous shall be seen, And a law for all generations and an enclosure shall be made for them.* (1 Enoch 93:6). Abraham is the man elected, his seed the plant, Sinai the law and the fence. And at the far end the charge to the sons is the same one Moses gave the plant at the Jordan: *But seek and choose for yourselves righteousness and an elect life, And walk in the paths of peace, And ye shall live and prosper.* (1 Enoch 94:4). Moses said it this way: *See, I have set before thee this day life and good, and death and evil;* (Deuteronomy 30:15), *I call heaven and earth to record this day against you, that I have set before you life and death, blessing and cursing: therefore choose life, that both thou and thy seed may live:* (Deuteronomy 30:19). The Psalter opens on the same fork: *Blessed is the man that walketh not in the counsel of the ungodly, nor standeth in the way of sinners, nor sitteth in the seat of the scornful.* (Psalms 1:1), and Yahusha (Jesus) gives it its narrow gate: *Enter ye in at the strait gate: for wide is the gate, and broad is the way, that leadeth to destruction, and many there be which go in thereat:* (Matthew 7:13). Sirach says it in one breath, *Before man is life and death; and whether him liketh shall be given him.* (Ecclesiasticus 15:17). The choice is set before a particular plant, the seed of the man who was elected, and it is the seed who are told to choose life so that they may be multiplied on the earth.
note: Invented 93:7 and 93:2 replaced by the live 93:2, 93:5-6 (the anchor span) and 94:4; retitled to what the live chapter carries; canon witnesses kept.

title: The paths of righteousness and the paths of violence — all who walk in unrighteousness shall perish
summary_md: Enoch's own count of the weeks begins with a warning about where the wrong road ends: *And after me there shall arise in the second week great wickedness, And deceit shall have sprung up; And in it there shall be the first end. And in it a man shall be saved; And after it is ended unrighteousness shall grow up, And a law shall be made for the sinners.* (1 Enoch 93:4). The flood was the first end, and Noah the man saved out of it. Just before the recounting he had set the two roads before his sons in so many words: *And now I tell you, my sons, and show you The paths of righteousness and the paths of violence. Yea, I will show them to you again That ye may know what will come to pass.* (1 Enoch 91:18), *And now, hearken unto me, my sons, And walk in the paths of righteousness, And walk not in the paths of violence; For all who walk in the paths of unrighteousness shall perish for ever.'* (1 Enoch 91:19). The Psalter's first song ends on the same verdict: *For Yahuah (LORD) knoweth the way of the righteous: but the way of the ungodly shall perish.* (Psalms 1:6). Solomon draws the two roads as light against dark: *But the path of the just is as the shining light, that shineth more and more unto the perfect day.* (Proverbs 4:18), *The way of the wicked is as darkness: they know not at what they stumble.* (Proverbs 4:19). Yahusha (Jesus) says which of the two has life at the end of it: *Because strait is the gate, and narrow is the way, which leadeth unto life, and few there be that find it.* (Matthew 7:14). And the Wisdom of Solomon lets the ungodly say it themselves on the day: *We wearied ourselves in the way of wickedness and destruction: yes, we have gone through deserts, where there lay no way: but as for the way of Yahuah (God), we have not known it.* (Wisdom of Solomon 5:7). The way of violence is not struck down by some arbitrary hand. It has no way in it, and the ones who walk it perish on it.
note: Invented 93:4 'cut off' replaced by the live 93:4 (anchor) and 91:18-19 where the two-paths words live; canon witnesses kept.

title: The apostate generation, and the elect righteous chosen for sevenfold instruction
summary_md: The seventh week is the one Enoch's sons live in: *And after that in the seventh week shall an apostate generation arise, And many shall be its deeds, And all its deeds shall be apostate.* (1 Enoch 93:9). And out of that generation, at its close, a company is chosen: *And at its close shall be elected The elect righteous of the eternal plant of righteousness, To receive sevenfold instruction concerning all His creation.* (1 Enoch 93:10). What the elect are instructed in is nothing other than the way the fathers walked, and the fathers named it as the two commandments. Jubilees has Noah charge his sons' sons *to bless their Creator, and honour father and mother, and love their neighbour* (Jubilees 7:20), and Abraham charge his house *that they should observe the way of Yahuah (God); that they should work righteousness, and love each his neighbour* (Jubilees 20:2). Moses gave the first of those its full weight: *And thou shalt love Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) with all thine heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy might.* (Deuteronomy 6:5), and Yahusha (Jesus) set the two side by side as the whole of it: *Yahusha (Jesus) said unto him, Thou shalt love Yahuah Elohayka (the Lord thy God) with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy mind.* (Matthew 22:37), *And the second is like unto it, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself.* (Matthew 22:39). An apostate generation is one that has let go of both. The elect righteous at the close of it are the plant of righteousness coming back to the instruction the plant was given at the start. It ain't new. The same love of Elohim (God) and neighbour runs from Enoch to Noah to Abraham to the one who called it the first and second commandment.
note: Invented 93:9-10 replaced by the live 93:9-10 (the anchor: apostate generation, elect righteous instructed); retitled; Jubilees, Deuteronomy, Matthew kept.

title: The plant of righteousness, the law, and the enclosure — judgment and righteousness as the way
summary_md: The third and fourth weeks are the planting and the fencing: *And after that in the third week at its close A man shall be elected as the plant of righteous judgement, And his posterity shall become the plant of righteousness for evermore.* (1 Enoch 93:5), *And after that in the fourth week, at its close, Visions of the holy and righteous shall be seen, And a law for all generations and an enclosure shall be made for them.* (1 Enoch 93:6). Abraham is elected as a plant of righteous judgment, which tells you what the plant is for, and the law given in the fourth week is the enclosure that keeps it. Micah summed up that law in a line: *He hath shewed thee, O man, what is good; and what doth Yahuah (LORD) require of thee, but to do justly, and to love mercy, and to walk humbly with thy Elohim (God)?* (Micah 6:8). Abraham's own house was charged with the same thing in the same words: *And he commanded them that they should observe the way of Yahuah (God); that they should work righteousness, and love each his neighbour, and act on this manner amongst all men; that they should each so walk with regard to them as to do judgment and righteousness on the earth.* (Jubilees 20:2). The Epistle's woes are what it looks like when the plant forgets the enclosure: *Woe to those who build unrighteousness and oppression And lay deceit as a foundation; For they shall be suddenly overthrown, And they shall have no peace.* (1 Enoch 94:6), and *Woe to you who devour the finest of the wheat, And drink wine in large bowls, And tread under foot the lowly with your might.* (1 Enoch 96:5). So the two ways here are not abstract. A plant elected for righteous judgment that tramples the lowly has left its own enclosure, and the humble walk is the fence it was given.
note: Invented 93:5-6 'paths of righteousness are these' replaced by the live 93:5-6 (anchor: plant and enclosure); the reworded 94:6 re-cited to the live 94:6 and 96:5; Micah 6:8 kept, Jubilees 20:2 added from the live pool.

title: The two ways — choose the paths of righteousness, that ye may live
summary_md: Enoch frames the whole Epistle as a choice between two roads: *And now I say unto you, my sons, love righteousness and walk therein; For the paths of righteousness are worthy of acceptation, But the paths of unrighteousness shall suddenly be destroyed and vanish.* (1 Enoch 94:1). He warns off the one road, *And now I say unto you the righteous: Walk not in the paths of wickedness, nor in the paths of death, And draw not nigh to them, lest ye be destroyed.* (1 Enoch 94:3), and sets the other in front of them: *But seek and choose for yourselves righteousness and an elect life, And walk in the paths of peace, And ye shall live and prosper.* (1 Enoch 94:4). This is Moses' summons at the edge of the land: *See, I have set before thee this day life and good, and death and evil* (Deuteronomy 30:15), *therefore choose life, that both thou and thy seed may live* (Deuteronomy 30:19). Jeremiah had the same two roads in his mouth: *Thus saith Yahuah (LORD); Behold, I set before you the way of life, and the way of death* (Jeremiah 21:8). The Psalter opens on it: *For Yahuah (LORD) knoweth the way of the righteous: but the way of the ungodly shall perish* (Psalm 1:6), and Proverbs paints the two in light and dark: *But the path of the just is as the shining light, that shineth more and more unto the perfect day* (Proverbs 4:18) against *The way of the wicked is as darkness: they know not at what they stumble* (Proverbs 4:19). Yahusha (Jesus) set the same fork before the crowds: *Enter ye in at the strait gate: for wide is the gate, and broad is the way, that leadeth to destruction, and many there be which go in thereat* (Matthew 7:13), *Because strait is the gate, and narrow is the way, which leadeth unto life, and few there be that find it* (Matthew 7:14). It is one summons from Sinai to Enoch to the mount where he sat down and taught. Walk the way that has life at the end of it.
note: 94:1 re-quoted from the live verse; the invented 94:23 replaced by the live 94:3-4; canon witnesses kept.

title: Woe to you who trust in your riches — they will not deliver in the day of affliction
summary_md: The woe is not on having money. It is on what the heart leaned on while the money was there: *Woe to you, ye rich, for ye have trusted in your riches, And from your riches shall ye depart, Because ye have not remembered the El Elyon (Most High) in the days of your riches.* (1 Enoch 94:8). The Epistle says later what that trust is worth when the day comes: *And (then) the children of the earth shall see the wise in security, And shall understand all the words of this book, And recognize that their riches shall not be able to save them In the overthrow of their sins.* (1 Enoch 100:6). The Psalter had already weighed it: *They that trust in their wealth, and boast themselves in the multitude of their riches* (Psalm 49:6), and found that *None of them can by any means redeem his brother, nor give to Elohim (God) a ransom for him* (Psalm 49:7), because *when he dieth he shall carry nothing away: his glory shall not descend after him* (Psalm 49:17). Yahusha (Jesus) told the story of one such man and let him speak for himself: *Soul, thou hast much goods laid up for many years; take thine ease, eat, drink, and be merry* (Luke 12:19), and then the answer, *Elohim (God) said unto him, Thou fool, this night thy soul shall be required of thee: then whose shall those things be, which thou hast provided?* (Luke 12:20). James says the same over the same departing wealth: *Go to now, ye rich men, weep and howl for your miseries that shall come upon you* (James 5:1). And the Wisdom of Solomon lets the rich say it themselves when it is too late: *What has pride profited us? or what good has riches with our vaunting brought us?* (Wisdom of Solomon 5:8). The riches depart and the man who did not remember the Most High in the good days has nothing left to remember him by in the bad ones.
note: Reworded 94:3 re-quoted from the live 94:8; invented 94:5 replaced by the live 100:6; Psalm 49, Luke 12, James 5, Wisdom kept.

title: Your riches shall not endure — the sinner's glory withers and goes into the furnace
summary_md: Enoch lets the rich man make his boast in full before he answers it: *Woe to you who acquire silver and gold in unrighteousness and say: 'We have become rich with riches and have possessions; And have acquired everything we have desired.* (1 Enoch 97:8), *And now let us do what we purposed: For we have gathered silver, And many are the husbandmen in our houses.' And our granaries are (brim) full as with water,* (1 Enoch 97:9). The answer is in the next breath: *Yea and like water your lies shall flow away; For your riches shall not abide But speedily ascend from you; For ye have acquired it all in unrighteousness, And ye shall be given over to a great curse.* (1 Enoch 97:10). And in the woes before it the house itself goes: *Woe to those who build their houses with sin; For from all their foundations shall they be overthrown, And by the sword shall they fall. [And those who acquire gold and silver in judgement suddenly shall perish.]* (1 Enoch 94:7). The end of the splendour is the furnace: *Therefore they shall be wanting in doctrine and wisdom, And they shall perish thereby together with their possessions; And with all their glory and their splendour, And in shame and in slaughter and in great destitution, Their spirits shall be cast into the furnace of fire.* (1 Enoch 98:3). Ben Sira had mocked the hoarder's plan long before: *Whereas he says, I have found rest, and now will eat continually of my goods; and yet he knoweth not what time shall come upon him, and that he must leave those things to others, and die* (Ecclesiasticus 11:19). The Psalter's picture of the wicked's end is the grass: *For they shall soon be cut down like the grass, and wither as the green herb* (Psalm 37:2), and *the wicked shall perish... into smoke shall they consume away* (Psalm 37:20). James sets the rust on the hoard as a witness of fire: *Your gold and silver is cankered; and the rust of them shall be a witness against you, and shall eat your flesh as it were fire. Ye have heaped treasure together for the last days* (James 5:3). Granaries full as with water, and lies that flow away like water. Enoch chose the same word for both on purpose.
note: The two reworded boasts re-quoted from the live 97:8-9; the invented 94:12 and 94:16 replaced by the live 97:10, 94:7 (anchor) and 98:3; canon witnesses kept.

title: Woe to you who feast in luxury and tread upon the poor
summary_md: The woes turn on the ones whose table is laid on other men's backs: *Woe to those who build unrighteousness and oppression And lay deceit as a foundation; For they shall be suddenly overthrown, And they shall have no peace.* (1 Enoch 94:6), and in the plainest picture of it, *Woe to you who devour the finest of the wheat, And drink wine in large bowls, And tread under foot the lowly with your might.* (1 Enoch 96:5). Isaiah had the same woe against the same appetite: *Woe unto them that join house to house, that lay field to field, till there be no place, that they may be placed alone in the midst of the earth!* (Isaiah 5:8), *Woe unto them that are mighty to drink wine, and men of strength to mingle strong drink* (Isaiah 5:22). Amos drew the very bowl: *That lie upon beds of ivory, and stretch themselves upon their couches, and eat the lambs out of the flock* (Amos 6:4), *That drink wine in bowls, and anoint themselves with the chief ointments: but they are not grieved for the affliction of Joseph* (Amos 6:6). Yahusha (Jesus) set the woe right beside the blessings: *But woe unto you that are rich! for ye have received your consolation* (Luke 6:24), *Woe unto you that are full! for ye shall hunger* (Luke 6:25), which is the Epistle's own sentence on the ones who spread harm to their neighbours: *Woe to you who spread evil to your neighbours; For you shall be slain in Sheol.* (1 Enoch 99:11). And James closes it: *Ye have lived in pleasure on the earth, and been wanton; ye have nourished your hearts, as in a day of slaughter* (James 5:5). The lowly trodden under foot are the ones the Lord of the whole thing is going to answer for, and the feast built on their backs is what gets overthrown.
note: Reworded 94:6/94:18 re-quoted from the live 94:6 and 96:5; invented 94:19 replaced by the live 99:11 (the anchor's far end); Isaiah, Amos, Luke, James kept.

title: Woe to those who pervert the words of uprightness and transgress the eternal law
summary_md: Enoch weeps before he pronounces anything: *Oh that mine eyes were [a cloud of] waters That I might weep over you, And pour down my tears as a cloud of waters: That so I might rest from my trouble of heart!* (1 Enoch 95:1), *Who has permitted you to practise reproaches and wickedness? And so judgement shall overtake you, sinners.* (1 Enoch 95:2). The woes that follow fall on the systems of deceit, and the sharpest of them is kept for the ones who rewrite the standard itself: *Woe to you who work godlessness, And glory in lying and extol them: Ye shall perish, and no happy life shall be yours.* (1 Enoch 99:1), *Woe to them who pervert the words of uprightness, And transgress the eternal law, And transform themselves into what they were not [into sinners]: They shall be trodden under foot upon the earth.* (1 Enoch 99:2). Isaiah's woes name the same inversion: *Woe unto them that call evil good, and good evil; that put darkness for light, and light for darkness; that put bitter for sweet, and sweet for bitter!* (Isaiah 5:20), *Woe unto them that are wise in their own eyes, and prudent in their own sight!* (Isaiah 5:21). Yahusha (Jesus) turned the same word on the self-satisfied of his day: *But woe unto you that are rich! for ye have received your consolation.* (Luke 6:24). Notice what Enoch calls the thing they pervert. It is the eternal law, and the ones who alter it do not become something new and better. They transform themselves into what they were not, which is sinners, and they write their own sentence in the act.
note: Reworded 95:1 and invented 95:2 replaced by the live 95:1-2 (anchor) and 99:1-2 where the perverted-words woe lives; Isaiah 5, Luke 6 kept.

title: Woe to the lying witnesses, the false weights, and those who persecute the righteous
summary_md: The heart of the chapter is a run of woes on the ways men wrong one another: *Woe to you who requite your neighbour with evil; For ye shall be requited according to your works.* (1 Enoch 95:5), *Woe to you, lying witnesses, And to those who weigh out injustice, For suddenly shall ye perish.* (1 Enoch 95:6), *Woe to you, sinners, for ye persecute the righteous; For ye shall be delivered up and persecuted because of injustice, And heavy shall its yoke be upon you.* (1 Enoch 95:7). The false balance and the false witness are the Torah's own list, and Amos saw both at work in the market: *Saying, When will the new moon be gone, that we may sell corn? and the sabbath, that we may set forth wheat, making the ephah small, and the shekel great, and falsifying the balances by deceit?* (Amos 8:5). Amos pronounced the same sentence on the ones at ease who did the weighing: *Woe to them that are at ease in Zion... That drink wine in bowls, and anoint themselves with the chief ointments: but they are not grieved for the affliction of Joseph. Therefore now shall they go captive with the first that go captive* (Amos 6:1,6,7). The Epistle keeps the gold in the same hands: *Woe to you who acquire silver and gold in unrighteousness and say: 'We have become rich with riches and have possessions; And have acquired everything we have desired.* (1 Enoch 97:8). James carries the cry of the defrauded into the last days: *Behold, the hire of the labourers who have reaped down your fields, which is of you kept back by fraud, crieth: and the cries of them which have reaped are entered into the ears of Yahuah (Lord) of sabaoth.* (James 5:4). Riches weighed out with a false measure cannot stand, *for he that getteth riches, and not by right... at his end shall be a fool.* (Jeremiah 17:11). Requited according to your works is the whole of it. The measure a man uses on his neighbour is the measure that comes back on him.
note: Invented 95:5 and reworded 95:6-7 replaced by the live 95:5-7 (anchor: requital, lying witnesses, false weights, persecution) and 97:8; retitled; Amos 8:5 added from the live pool; Amos 6, James 5, Jeremiah 17 kept.

title: Where are your riches now? — the rich man's wealth perishes
summary_md: Enoch's tears open the chapter, *Oh that mine eyes were [a cloud of] waters That I might weep over you, And pour down my tears as a cloud of waters: That so I might rest from my trouble of heart!* (1 Enoch 95:1), and the Epistle goes on to stage the reckoning those tears are for: *Therefore they shall be wanting in doctrine and wisdom, And they shall perish thereby together with their possessions; And with all their glory and their splendour, And in shame and in slaughter and in great destitution, Their spirits shall be cast into the furnace of fire.* (1 Enoch 98:3). The Parables let the mighty say what they see when it is gone: *For we have not believed before Him Nor glorified the name of Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits, [nor glorified our Lord] But our hope was in the sceptre of our kingdom, And in our glory.* (1 Enoch 63:7), *Now they shall say unto themselves: 'Our souls are full of unrighteous gain, but it does not prevent us from descending from the midst thereof into the burden of Sheol.'* (1 Enoch 63:10), which is the Epistle's own woe: *Woe to you who spread evil to your neighbours; For you shall be slain in Sheol.* (1 Enoch 99:11). Yahusha (Jesus) told the scene as a story: *And I will say to my soul, Soul, thou hast much goods laid up for many years; take thine ease, eat, drink, and be merry. But Elohim (God) said unto him, Thou fool, this night thy soul shall be required of thee: then whose shall those things be, which thou hast provided?* (Luke 12:19-20). That is the boast of the full granaries answered by the night of demand. And the Wisdom of Solomon puts the confession in the mouths of the proud when they have perished: *What has pride profited us? or what good has riches with our vaunting brought us? All those things are passed away like a shadow* (Wisdom of Solomon 5:8-9). Unrighteous gain fills the soul and does nothing at all to keep it out of Sheol.
note: Invented 95:12-13 replaced by the live 95:1 (anchor), 98:3, 63:7, 63:10, 99:11; Luke 12 and Wisdom kept.

title: Fear not the sinners, ye righteous — the two paths and the way that lives
summary_md: Enoch's woes are spoken through tears, *Oh that mine eyes were [a cloud of] waters That I might weep over you, And pour down my tears as a cloud of waters: That so I might rest from my trouble of heart!* (1 Enoch 95:1), and in the middle of them he turns to the righteous: *Fear not the sinners, ye righteous; For again will Yahuah (Lord) deliver them into your hands, That ye may execute judgement upon them according to your desires.* (1 Enoch 95:3). The choice that governs the whole Epistle was set out before the woes began: *And now, hearken unto me, my sons, And walk in the paths of righteousness, And walk not in the paths of violence; For all who walk in the paths of unrighteousness shall perish for ever.'* (1 Enoch 91:19), *But seek and choose for yourselves righteousness and an elect life, And walk in the paths of peace, And ye shall live and prosper.* (1 Enoch 94:4). That is Moses' covenant charge, life set against death with the seed's blessing hanging on it: *See, I have set before thee this day life and good, and death and evil;* (Deuteronomy 30:15), *I call heaven and earth to record this day against you, that I have set before you life and death, blessing and cursing: therefore choose life, that both thou and thy seed may live:* (Deuteronomy 30:19). The Psalter opens on the same two roads: *Blessed is the man that walketh not in the counsel of the ungodly... For Yahuah (LORD) knoweth the way of the righteous: but the way of the ungodly shall perish.* (Psalm 1:1,6), and Proverbs lights the difference: *But the path of the just is as the shining light, that shineth more and more unto the perfect day. The way of the wicked is as darkness* (Proverbs 4:18-19). The way of violence perishes for ever, and the ones who walk the other road are told not to be afraid of the ones on it.
note: Invented 95:17-18 replaced by the live 95:1 and 95:3 (anchor) with the two-paths charge from 91:19 and 94:4; canon witnesses kept.

title: Woe to those who tread on the lowly with their might
summary_md: The first woe in the chapter is on the ones whose money makes them look like the righteous: *Woe unto you, ye sinners, for your riches make you appear like the righteous, But your hearts convict you of being sinners, And this fact shall be a testimony against you for a memorial of (your) evil deeds.* (1 Enoch 96:4), and the next is on what that money was built on: *Woe to you who devour the finest of the wheat, And drink wine in large bowls, And tread under foot the lowly with your might.* (1 Enoch 96:5). The prophets had already named the crime. Amos: *Forasmuch therefore as your treading is upon the poor, and ye take from him burdens of wheat: ye have built houses of hewn stone, but ye shall not dwell in them; ye have planted pleasant vineyards, but ye shall not drink wine of them.* (Amos 5:11), and *they afflict the just, they take a bribe, and they turn aside the poor in the gate from their right.* (Amos 5:12). Isaiah carries it to the rulers who ate the vineyard: *Yahuah (LORD) will enter into judgment with the ancients of his people, and the princes thereof: for ye have eaten up the vineyard; the spoil of the poor is in your houses.* (Isaiah 3:14), *What mean ye that ye beat my people to pieces, and grind the faces of the poor? saith Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD) of hosts.* (Isaiah 3:15). And the Torah's own protection of the afflicted stands behind every one of these woes: *Rob not the poor, because he is poor: neither oppress the afflicted in the gate:* (Proverbs 22:22), because *Yahuah (LORD) will plead their cause, and spoil the soul of those that spoiled them.* (Proverbs 22:23). Riches can make a man look righteous. The one who treads the lowly under foot has a heart that convicts him, and Enoch says that heart is the memorial that will be read.
note: Invented 96:1 replaced by the live 96:4 and 96:5 (the reworded 96:4 re-quoted in full); Amos, Isaiah, Proverbs kept.

title: Woe to the mighty who oppress the righteous — the day of your destruction is coming
summary_md: Enoch's woes are bracketed by comfort to the ones being trodden on. He begins, *Be hopeful, ye righteous; for suddenly shall the sinners perish before you, And ye shall have lordship over them according to your desires.* (1 Enoch 96:1), and *Wherefore fear not, ye that have suffered; For healing shall be your portion, And a bright light shall enlighten you, And the voice of rest ye shall hear from heaven.* (1 Enoch 96:3). Then the woe on the strong: *Woe to you, ye mighty, Who with might oppress the righteous; For the day of your destruction is coming. In those days many and good days shall come to the righteous—in the day of your judgement.* (1 Enoch 96:8), and on the ones who forsook the only fountain, *Woe to you who drink water from every fountain, For suddenly shall ye be consumed and wither away, Because ye have forsaken the fountain of life.* (1 Enoch 96:6). Yahusha (Jesus) spoke the same reversal in almost the same words: *But woe unto you that are rich! for ye have received your consolation.* (Luke 6:24), *Woe unto you that are full! for ye shall hunger. Woe unto you that laugh now! for ye shall mourn and weep.* (Luke 6:25). James says it over the hoard: *Go to now, ye rich men, weep and howl for your miseries that shall come upon you.* (James 5:1), *Your gold and silver is cankered; and the rust of them shall be a witness against you, and shall eat your flesh as it were fire. Ye have heaped treasure together for the last days.* (James 5:3). And the Wisdom of Solomon lets the mighty confess it afterward: *What has pride profited us? or what good has riches with our vaunting brought us?* (Wisdom of Solomon 5:8), *All those things are passed away like a shadow, and as a post that hasted by;* (Wisdom of Solomon 5:9). The day of the mighty man's destruction and the good days of the righteous are the same day. That is why the righteous are told to be hopeful and the mighty are told woe.
note: Invented 96:2-3 replaced by the live 96:1, 96:3, 96:6, 96:8 (anchor span); Luke 6, James 5, Wisdom kept.

title: The mighty who oppress the righteous, and the furnace at the end of their splendour
summary_md: The last woe of the chapter is on strength used against the righteous: *Woe to you, ye mighty, Who with might oppress the righteous; For the day of your destruction is coming. In those days many and good days shall come to the righteous—in the day of your judgement.* (1 Enoch 96:8). The Epistle tells where that strength ends: *For ye men shall put on more adornments than a woman, And coloured garments more than a virgin: In royalty and in grandeur and in power, And in silver and in gold and in purple, And in splendour and in food they shall be poured out as water.* (1 Enoch 98:2), *Therefore they shall be wanting in doctrine and wisdom, And they shall perish thereby together with their possessions; And with all their glory and their splendour, And in shame and in slaughter and in great destitution, Their spirits shall be cast into the furnace of fire.* (1 Enoch 98:3). James hears the cry of the ones whose labour paid for the purple: *Behold, the hire of the labourers who have reaped down your fields, which is of you kept back by fraud, crieth: and the cries of them which have reaped are entered into the ears of Yahuah (Lord) of sabaoth.* (James 5:4), and names the end of the oppression, *Ye have condemned and killed the just; and he doth not resist you.* (James 5:6). Ben Sira calls the withheld wage what it is: *He that takes away his neighbour's living slayeth him; and he that defraudeth the labourer of his hire is a bloodshedder.* (Ecclesiasticus 34:22). And the Wisdom of Solomon watches the proud blow away: *For the hope of the ungodly is like dust that is blown away with the wind; like a thin froth that is driven away with the storm; like as the smoke which is dispersed here and there with a tempest, and passeth away as the remembrance of a guest that tarrieth but a day.* (Wisdom of Solomon 5:14). Poured out as water, and gone like smoke. The righteous they oppressed get their many and good days on the very day the mighty are judged.
note: Invented 96:8-10 replaced by the live 96:8 (anchor) and 98:2-3; James, Sirach, Wisdom kept.

title: Be hopeful, ye righteous — the two paths and the fountain of life
summary_md: The chapter opens on hope for the ones on the right road: *Be hopeful, ye righteous; for suddenly shall the sinners perish before you, And ye shall have lordship over them according to your desires.* (1 Enoch 96:1), *Wherefore fear not, ye that have suffered; For healing shall be your portion, And a bright light shall enlighten you, And the voice of rest ye shall hear from heaven.* (1 Enoch 96:3). The other road is named by what it drinks from: *Woe to you who drink water from every fountain, For suddenly shall ye be consumed and wither away, Because ye have forsaken the fountain of life.* (1 Enoch 96:6). Enoch had set the two roads before his sons at the start of the Epistle: *And now, hearken unto me, my sons, And walk in the paths of righteousness, And walk not in the paths of violence; For all who walk in the paths of unrighteousness shall perish for ever.'* (1 Enoch 91:19), *But seek and choose for yourselves righteousness and an elect life, And walk in the paths of peace, And ye shall live and prosper.* (1 Enoch 94:4). That is Moses' charge at the Jordan: *See, I have set before thee this day life and good, and death and evil;* (Deuteronomy 30:15), *In that I command thee this day to love Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God), to walk in his ways, and to keep his commandments and his statutes and his judgments, that thou mayest live and multiply: and Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) shall bless thee in the land whither thou goest to possess it.* (Deuteronomy 30:16), *therefore choose life, that both thou and thy seed may live:* (Deuteronomy 30:19). The forsaken fountain is the one Jeremiah wept over: *For my people have committed two evils; they have forsaken me the fountain of living waters, and hewed them out cisterns, broken cisterns, that can hold no water.* (Jeremiah 2:13). And the Psalter sets the same two roads: *Blessed is the man that walketh not in the counsel of the ungodly, nor standeth in the way of sinners, nor sitteth in the seat of the scornful.* (Psalms 1:1), *For Yahuah (LORD) knoweth the way of the righteous: but the way of the ungodly shall perish.* (Psalms 1:6). One road drinks from every fountain and withers. The other is told to be hopeful, because healing and light and rest are its portion.
note: Invented 96:15-16 replaced by the live 96:1, 96:3, 96:6 (anchor span) and the two-paths charge at 91:19 and 94:4; Jeremiah 2:13 added from the live pool; Deuteronomy 30 and Psalm 1 kept.

title: We have become rich — the riches that testify against the rich
summary_md: Enoch lets the unrighteous rich make their speech, and the speech is the evidence: *Woe to you who acquire silver and gold in unrighteousness and say: 'We have become rich with riches and have possessions; And have acquired everything we have desired.* (1 Enoch 97:8), *And now let us do what we purposed: For we have gathered silver, And many are the husbandmen in our houses.' And our granaries are (brim) full as with water,* (1 Enoch 97:9). The answer turns their own picture on them: *Yea and like water your lies shall flow away; For your riches shall not abide But speedily ascend from you; For ye have acquired it all in unrighteousness, And ye shall be given over to a great curse.* (1 Enoch 97:10). And the day it is all read out: *And all the words of your unrighteousness shall be read out before the Great Holy One, And your faces shall be covered with shame, And He will reject every work which is grounded on unrighteousness.* (1 Enoch 97:6). James hears the hoard itself give testimony: *Your gold and silver is cankered; and the rust of them shall be a witness against you, and shall eat your flesh as it were fire. Ye have heaped treasure together for the last days.* (James 5:3). Habakkuk had raised the taunt already: *Shall not all these take up a parable against him, and a taunting proverb against him, and say, Woe to him that increaseth that which is not his! how long? and to him that ladeth himself with thick clay!* (Habakkuk 2:6). Yahusha (Jesus) calls it what it is on the night it is exposed: *But Elohim (God) said unto him, Thou fool, this night thy soul shall be required of thee: then whose shall those things be, which thou hast provided?* (Luke 12:20). And the proverb gives the verdict Enoch is pronouncing: *Riches profit not in the day of wrath: but righteousness delivereth from death.* (Proverbs 11:4). The woe is on the acquiring in unrighteousness, not on possessing. The wealth gathered that way keeps a record of how it was gathered, and the record is read.
note: Reworded 97:7 re-quoted from the live 97:8-9; invented 97:14-15 replaced by the live 97:10 and 97:6; James, Habakkuk, Luke, Proverbs kept.

title: The prayer of the righteous reaches the Lord — and the days of your judgement come
summary_md: The sinners are asked a question they cannot answer: *What will ye do, ye sinners, And whither will ye flee on that day of judgement, When ye hear the voice of the prayer of the righteous?* (1 Enoch 97:3), *And in those days the prayer of the righteous shall reach unto Yahuah (Lord), And for you the days of your judgement shall come.* (1 Enoch 97:5), *And all the words of your unrighteousness shall be read out before the Great Holy One, And your faces shall be covered with shame, And He will reject every work which is grounded on unrighteousness.* (1 Enoch 97:6). The ones praying are the ones the Epistle has just shown trodden under foot: *Woe to you who devour the finest of the wheat, And drink wine in large bowls, And tread under foot the lowly with your might.* (1 Enoch 96:5). Amos drew that table, the couch, the feast, the bowl of wine, with the poor uncared for in the next room: *That lie upon beds of ivory, and stretch themselves upon their couches, and eat the lambs out of the flock, and the calves out of the midst of the stall;* (Amos 6:4), *That drink wine in bowls, and anoint themselves with the chief ointments: but they are not grieved for the affliction of Joseph.* (Amos 6:6). Isaiah ties the strong drinker to the cry of the oppressed: *Woe unto them that are mighty to drink wine, and men of strength to mingle strong drink:* (Isaiah 5:22), having already wept that the vineyard yielded *oppression... a cry* instead of judgement (Isaiah 5:7). James gives the cry a voice and an address: *Behold, the hire of the labourers who have reaped down your fields, which is of you kept back by fraud, crieth: and the cries of them which have reaped are entered into the ears of Yahuah (Lord) of sabaoth.* (James 5:4). The reapers' cry enters the ears of the Lord of hosts. Enoch calls it the prayer of the righteous reaching him, and says the day it arrives is the day the judgement of the ones at the table begins.
note: Invented 97:5 and reworded 97:6 replaced by the live 97:3, 97:5, 97:6 (anchor) with 96:5 for the bowls; retitled to the live anchor; Amos, Isaiah, James kept.

title: The sinners will become a shame and perish — the end of the splendour
summary_md: The chapter opens with a word to the righteous to believe what they cannot yet see: *Believe, ye righteous, that the sinners will become a shame And perish in the day of unrighteousness.* (1 Enoch 97:1), *Be it known unto you (ye sinners) that the El Elyon (Most High) is mindful of your destruction, And the angels of heaven rejoice over your destruction.* (1 Enoch 97:2). The Epistle has already described the splendour that goes into the fire: *For ye men shall put on more adornments than a woman, And coloured garments more than a virgin: In royalty and in grandeur and in power, And in silver and in gold and in purple, And in splendour and in food they shall be poured out as water.* (1 Enoch 98:2), *Therefore they shall be wanting in doctrine and wisdom, And they shall perish thereby together with their possessions; And with all their glory and their splendour, And in shame and in slaughter and in great destitution, Their spirits shall be cast into the furnace of fire.* (1 Enoch 98:3). And the woe that stands behind it: *Woe to you, ye rich, for ye have trusted in your riches, And from your riches shall ye depart, Because ye have not remembered the El Elyon (Most High) in the days of your riches.* (1 Enoch 94:8). The Wisdom of Solomon puts the lament in the mouths of the perished: *What has pride profited us? or what good has riches with our vaunting brought us?* (Wisdom of Solomon 5:8), and likens what they hoped in to dust: *For the hope of the ungodly is like dust that is blown away with the wind; like a thin froth that is driven away with the storm; like as the smoke which is dispersed here and there with a tempest, and passeth away as the remembrance of a guest that tarrieth but a day.* (Wisdom of Solomon 5:14). The purple and the grandeur are real while they last. Enoch's point is that the righteous should believe the end of them before it arrives, because the Most High is already mindful of it.
note: Invented 97:11-12 and 94:4 replaced by the live 97:1-2 (anchor), 98:2-3, 94:8; retitled; Wisdom kept.
